candidates.title: cartesi-machine CLI aborts --mcycle-computation-hash / --uarch-cycle-computation-hash runs (no claim computed) when a guest accepts with an outputs-root length other than 32 bytes
candidates.component: cartesi-machine CLI (src/cartesi-machine.lua), cmio advance-state driver used by its computation-hash options
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'the cartesi-machine CLI ... Support'). Its --mcycle-computation-hash and --uarch-cycle-computation-hash options are a tool that computes claims, so section 3 lets it stand in for the honest operator.
candidates.location: src/cartesi-machine.lua flush_pending_outputs (line 3689: assert(#data == cartesi.HASH_SIZE, "expected outputs Merkle root in tx buffer")), called unconditionally from run_advance_state_input (line 4723) for every rx-accepted manual yield, whatever builder is selected (new_mcycle_computation_hash_builder / new_uarch_cycle_computation_hash_builder). Also line 3692-3696 (check_outputs_merkle_root, default true, aborts on any outputs-root mismatch).
candidates.description: On every rx-accepted manual yield the CLI reads data = receive_cmio_request() (length = min(htif_tohost DATA field, tx buffer length)) and asserts #data == 32. The transition function does not interpret that length: section 4 says 'The outputs Merkle root, the output payloads, and every other yield reason are opaque guest data that the state merely commits to', and A5 extracts the root from the first tx-buffer word regardless of the declared length (the PRT player does exactly that, reading machine:read_memory(CMIO_TX_BUFFER_ADDRESS, 32)). A guest that yields rx-accepted with DATA 0, 1..31, 33.., or 0xffffffff (clamped to 2 MiB) is still at an accepted fixed point that the next delivery advances, so the epoch's mcycle claim and every uarch claim are well defined. The CLI instead raises a Lua error in the middle of the epoch, before builder:end_input / end_epoch, so the computation hash is never reported and the process exits 1. There is no option to disable the check (check_outputs_merkle_root:false only disables the root comparison, not the length assert), so for such a guest the CLI cannot compute the claim at all. With the default check_outputs_merkle_root:true the same abort happens for any guest whose root does not match the host's outputs tree (a wrong root, or outputs the guest emitted but did not fold in). By contrast, the CLI's own help says unexpected fixed points (halt, overflow, exception, unexpected manual yield) still finalize the computation hash, and the PRT player computes the correct claim for the same guest (verified).
candidates.trigger: Any application whose guest (or an input that took control of it, section 4) writes htif tohost = (dev YIELD, cmd MANUAL, reason RX_ACCEPTED, data != 32), e.g. a bare-metal or custom-runtime guest that writes the root word and yields with length 0. The party running the CLI to compute the claim of that epoch is the victim.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from a valid template: the yield DATA field is guest-writable (any value is presumed reachable, section 2 'Reachable state'). Demonstrated with a bare-metal guest built by the harness builder.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is an application that is not correctly designed ('When it accepts, it leaves in the tx buffer the outputs Merkle root' - a length != 32 arguably breaks the rollup interface). Section 8 excludes 'what such an application gets', but: 'An application that breaks the rollup interface may leave its outputs unprovable, but it must never stop the honest operator from computing claims or producing proofs. Development tools may instead stop and report the violation.' So the trigger is not excluded for a component that computes claims; whether the CLI may stop depends on whether it is read as a 'development tool' (reading B) or as a claim-computing tool standing in for the honest operator (reading A). 2. Role: Support (AUDIT.md table). Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator or a tool that computes claims.' 3. High/Medium cases: in the stood-in honest-operator role it matches none of the High cases (not an unreachable state, not a cost factor). 4. Critical in the stood-in role: R4 'From any reachable state ... the honest operator can always compute the claim ... This holds for every guest, whether or not its application is correctly designed'. Failing to compute the claim is the Completeness failure of section 1 ('The honest operator ... cannot respond'). Critical in the stood-in role, capped at Medium for support. 5. Under reading B ('Development tools may instead stop and report the violation'; the assert message is a report) it is Low. Facts that decide: whether the CLI's computation-hash options (documented in the manual's 'Computation hashes' section as computing the dispute claims) count as 'a tool that computes claims' or as a development tool.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (reading A: support tool that computes claims, stood-in R4 Critical) / Low (reading B: development tool allowed to stop and report)
candidates.threat_to_goal: If an operator computed its claim with the CLI (the manual presents --mcycle-computation-hash as the way to compute the epoch claim), any guest that yields rx-accepted with a non-32 length (or, with defaults, a wrong root) would leave the honest operator without a claim; any claim, including a fabricated final state, could then win (section 8: 'If it stopped, any claim could win'). The PRT player handles the same guest correctly, so no production path is shown to be affected.
candidates.evidence: Built a chaos bare-metal guest (scratch RGPLAYERGUEST/chaos.c, op 'z' = write the correct root to the tx buffer and yield rx-accepted with DATA 0; 'Z' = DATA 0xffffffff). Template = chaos.bin run to its first rx-accepted yield. `cartesi-machine --load=<template> --revert-mode=none --cmio-advance-state=input:input-%i.bin,input_file_index_begin:0,input_file_index_end:2,check_outputs_merkle_root:false --mcycle-computation-hash=log2_mcycle_period:10` with input-0='oz', input-1='a' prints 'Manual yield rx-accepted (1) (0x000000 data)' then dies: 'cartesi-machine.lua:3689: expected outputs Merkle root in tx buffer' (traceback through flush_pending_outputs <- run_advance_state_input <- run_advance_state_epoch); no 'Mcycle computation hash' line. Same with --uarch-cycle-computation-hash and input-0='oZ' (exit 1). The forked PRT player (prt.new_forked_player) on the same template and inputs ['oOrRpuctfa','oz','oZ'] produces a claim whose root equals an independently assembled reference (collect_mcycle_root_hashes per input, rejection exception applied) - only an outputs_merkle_root_mismatch anomaly is reported. Differential harness (scratch RGPLAYERGUEST/diff.lua, chaos.c): for the forked player, scenarios ['oOrRpuctfa','oz','oZ'], ['Wa','ox','oX','a'], ['oyYa','lTx','ola'], ['oE','a'], ['oG','a'], ['oM','a'], ['oH','a'], ['ccccccccx','a'], ['ox','a'], ['oyYa','pux','a'] and, with a template at mcycle 2^64-6e6 (overflow at MCYCLE_MAX), ['oa','oa','oa','a'], ['S'], ['lllx','S'] all gave player claim root == reference root, matching sampled leaves, and verifying prove_state_transition logs at the stopping mcycles, at period 0, and at the first automatic-yield mcycle. The stored player (prt.new_stored_player) on ['oOrRpuctfa','oz','oZ','ox'] matched as well (claim root, leaves, uarch proofs of 5 periods). So the only guest-triggered failure found in the claim paths is the CLI's.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh: build the chaos guest (or a 10-line guest that writes the empty outputs root to the tx buffer and yields manual RX_ACCEPTED with DATA 0 for every input), store its template, run the CLI with --cmio-advance-state (one input, check_outputs_merkle_root:false) and --mcycle-computation-hash=log2_mcycle_period:10,filename:mch.bin. Required behavior: exit status 0 and mch.bin equal to the root the PRT player (prt.new_forked_player + commit_mcycle_claim) computes for the same template and input. Today: Lua assertion, no mch.bin -> exit 1.

candidates.title: crisium exits by assert and crash-loops once an epoch whose guest stopped at a non-accepted fixed point (halt, exception, unknown manual yield, imcyclemax) finishes its tournament
candidates.component: PRT player process: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:prepare (stageTournamentResult -> self.terminal) and doc/recipes/crisium.lua main loop (assert(not status.terminal, status.terminal))
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: the PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua lines 538-547 (pcall(eth.validity_proof, ...) failure sets self.terminal); doc/recipes/crisium.lua lines 316 and 373 (status.terminal -> assert, process exit); prt-supervise.sh relaunches and the same pass fails again.
candidates.description: When the honest claim wins an epoch whose final state is a halt, an exception yield, a manual yield with any reason other than accepted/rejected, or an imcyclemax stop, the bridge's stageTournamentResult job calls eth.validity_proof, which (correctly) refuses the final state; the bridge then sets terminal and crisium raises an assertion after the pass. On every relaunch the reopened epoch produces the same job and the process dies again, so the honest player stops doing anything else in that process (bond recovery, cleanup jobs) for good.
candidates.trigger: Any guest that ends an epoch at a non-accepted fixed point (e.g. halts on some input).
candidates.reachability: Reachable: a guest halt or exception yield is presumed reachable. The terminal state arises only after the root tournament is finished.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: the trigger is 'The stall of an application that halts, yields manually with a reason other than accepted or rejected, or never yields, and what the application loses by it. A5 governs what can then be extracted from its state.' DaveConsensus seals epoch N+1 only on acceptStagedTournamentResult of epoch N, so no later dispute exists that the crash could stop; the dispute of epoch N was already decided. 2. Role: Support. 3-4. If read as an emulator-side defect triggered by a guest ('The entries about applications exclude what an application loses, never an emulator defect that its guest triggers'), the stood-in honest operator crashes on its path, but no claim, node or proof is still owed (R4 holds), so no rule is violated. 5. Low at most (lost bond recovery for the honest submitter, which the model does not cover).
candidates.threat_to_goal: None to settlement: the epoch is decided and no later epoch can open. It only shows that the player turns an expected application stall into a permanent process crash loop instead of reporting it and idling.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only (prt-bridge.lua prepare, crisium.lua pass/main loop, game-output.lua validate_outputs_merkle_root_response asserting dev/cmd/reason). Not run on the chain harness.
candidates.test_idea: Unit-level: construct a bridge with a fake chain whose root tournament is finished with the player's claim as winner and a player whose outputs_merkle_root_proof proves a halted final state; call tick() and assert that bridge.terminal stays nil (or that crisium's pass returns a non-terminal status) while the anomaly is reported.

not_covered: End-to-end runs of crisium + bridge on the local chain with misbehaving guests (only the forked and stored players were driven directly through their event handlers, without the chain or the referee model).

Stored player (prt.new_stored_player): only one misbehaving scenario (['oOrRpuctfa','oz','oZ','ox']) was run to completion of the claim and 5 uarch periods (all matched); restart/reopen in the middle of misbehaving inputs and the agreed-pair idle advancement were not exercised.

Uarch-level checks were sampled: for each input, the period where the input stops (mcycles at and after the stopping instruction) and period 0, at uarch positions {0,1,2,100,1000,3000,20000,2^20-2,2^20-1}, by verifying prove_state_transition logs (verify_send_cmio_response / verify_step_uarch / verify_reset_uarch) against the player's own neighbouring leaves; uarch roots were not compared against an independent per-uarch-step reference (get_root_hash after each uarch step costs ~20 ms on these machines, too slow).

The mcycle-level reference uses the emulator's collect_mcycle_root_hashes (bundle 0) per input, so it checks the player's Lua padding, bundling, rejection and frontier logic, not the C++ collector itself.

Guests that never yield at the real geometry (2^48 mcycles per input) were only exercised through a template with mcycle near 2^64 (overflow at MCYCLE_MAX); the 'e' op (trap loop to an unmapped mtvec) was not completed for the same reason.
gio requests were exercised only as manual yields with a gio domain (fixed point); libcmt/rollup tools' own gio handling inside Linux was not run.
vg.lua honest player (verification game) under misbehaving guests beyond reading (its outputs-root abort is already R1-R8-2).

cartesi-machine --print-mcycle-root-hashes / --print-uarch-cycle-root-hashes with misbehaving guests outside cmio mode (rejection variants already R1-R6-1 and R3-VARSPEC-4); --assert-rolling-template with an rx-accepted yield of length != 32 (it reports 'not a template' although the tx-buffer word holds the root, a diagnostic difference not reported).
Heavy console output cost and host-channel behaviour inside crisium (stdout of spawned servers) was not measured.
Templates with unusual HTIF configurations (automatic yields disabled, iconsole variants) were not run through the player.
